facts.detail: Every UK home and business has a legal right to request a decent, affordable broadband connection subject to the scheme rules.
A decent connection is defined as at least 10 Mbit/s download and 1 Mbit/s upload.
Requests are made to BT, or KCOM in the Hull area.
An applicant does not need to be an existing BT or KCOM customer.

guard_streams.write_limit: A statutory request right is not evidence that a parcel already has an orderable or active connection.

facts.detail: BT or KCOM has 30 days to confirm eligibility and the estimated build cost.
Eligibility requires no existing decent broadband and no relevant public broadband scheme expected within the next 12 months.
If the applicant's share of build or upgrade cost is £3,400 or less, the applicant does not pay for the network work.
Most accepted connections are expected within 12 months, although some can take up to 24 months.

guard_streams.write_limit: Eligibility and delivery windows are workflow states, not current parcel coverage or measured speed.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom broadband and mobile coverage checker

facts.detail: The checker accepts a postcode and reports mobile coverage by provider and broadband availability for standard, superfast and ultrafast services.
Checker results can also be viewed through interactive maps.
Ofcom makes fixed-broadband and mobile data available to developers through APIs.
The coverage checker cannot report maintenance or known local incidents; customers should consult provider status information.

guard_streams.write_limit: Checker categories and APIs are availability evidence only and must not be treated as live outage or incident telemetry.

facts.detail: The checker uses Ordnance Survey property data and updates the base dataset twice a year.
No displayed prediction does not necessarily mean broadband is unavailable; network websites should also be checked.
FWA coverage uses operator predictive modelling and local conditions can prevent service at a particular premise despite a positive prediction.
A predicted service may be temporarily unavailable because of access permissions, maintenance, upgrades or other operational reasons.

guard_streams.write_limit: Predictions, missing records and provider listings cannot be promoted without an exact accepted parcel-level join and retained evidence.

facts.detail: Under One Touch Switch the customer contacts the gaining provider, which arranges the broadband switch.
A customer switching before contract end may face early termination charges and is told about applicable charges during the process.
The gaining provider requires service details, the address and the current provider to match the switch.
When the new service is working, the old broadband service ends automatically.

guard_streams.write_limit: A successful switching workflow confirms account movement, not underlying network technology, coverage or measured parcel speed.

facts.detail: The landline switch request includes whether the customer wants to retain the telephone number.
The gaining provider arranges the switch for the preferred date where possible.
The old provider must not charge for a notice period after the switching date.
Loss of service must not exceed one working day and compensation applies when defined switching or appointment failures occur.

guard_streams.write_limit: Number retention and switching compensation are consumer-process records, not broadband availability evidence.

facts.detail: The May 2026 redesign revised the Cambridgeshire contract to around 35,000 premises.
The redesigned contract is backed by up to £77 million of Project Gigabit investment.
The redesign followed significant commercial rollout expansion and changed market conditions.
Preparatory construction such as trenches, duct and fibre installation is required before residents or businesses can request service.

guard_streams.write_limit: A redesigned contract scope and planned build do not establish current orderability for any listed parcel.

facts.detail: The May 2026 Kent redesign revised the contract to around 9,000 premises.
The revised Kent contract is backed by £26.1 million of Project Gigabit investment.
The redesign aims to reduce overlap with suppliers' commercial rollout and focus subsidy on premises otherwise likely to miss out.
Premises in the contract remain subject to change through detailed planning or technical constraints.

guard_streams.write_limit: Regional contract inclusion is planned programme scope, not proof of present service or completion.

guard_streams.source: BDUK East and West Sussex Project Gigabit contract

facts.detail: The May 2026 East and West Sussex redesign revised the contract to around 13,000 premises.
The revised contract is backed by £25.2 million of Project Gigabit investment.
BDUK states that it is discussing remaining uncovered premises with other suppliers.
A premise may be outside the project because coverage already exists, a commercial or voucher plan exists, or delivery cost and difficulty are too high.

guard_streams.write_limit: Regional plans and alternative-supplier discussions must not be promoted as completed parcel coverage.

guard_streams.source: BDUK Buckinghamshire Hertfordshire East Berkshire contract

facts.detail: The May 2026 redesign revised the Buckinghamshire, Hertfordshire and East Berkshire contract to around 6,000 premises.
The revised contract is backed by £24.4 million of Project Gigabit investment.
The original award targeted around 34,000 hard-to-reach premises.
Residents and businesses can request a connection only after the gigabit-capable network has been built.

guard_streams.write_limit: Original or redesigned counts are programme estimates and cannot identify a currently serviceable parcel.

guard_streams.source: BDUK Nottinghamshire and West Lincolnshire contract

facts.detail: CityFibre is no longer delivering the Nottinghamshire and West Lincolnshire Project Gigabit contract.
BDUK and CityFibre mutually agreed to end the contract.
The stated reasons include wider market conditions and significant expansion of commercial rollout, reducing the need for public funding.
BDUK is discussing alternative suppliers for remaining premises not covered by rollout plans.

guard_streams.write_limit: A terminated contract and supplier discussions leave parcel status unresolved until replacement delivery evidence exists.

facts.detail: FullFibre is no longer delivering the Peak District Project Gigabit contract.
BDUK and FullFibre mutually agreed to terminate the contract.
BDUK states that it is putting alternative supplier plans in place for affected premises.
In April 2026 the Peak District area was added to Openreach call-off one, which covers parts of Staffordshire.

guard_streams.write_limit: Reassignment changes the delivery vehicle but does not prove that any individual premise is built or orderable.

guard_streams.source: BDUK West Herefordshire and Forest of Dean contract

facts.detail: BDUK and FullFibre mutually agreed to terminate the West Herefordshire and Forest of Dean contract.
BDUK states that alternative supplier plans are being developed for premises due to be covered.
In April 2026 West Herefordshire premises were included in Openreach call-off three.
The published reassignment specifically names West Herefordshire and does not state that Forest of Dean premises were included in that call-off.

guard_streams.write_limit: The geographic wording must be preserved; do not infer Forest of Dean reassignment or completed coverage.

facts.detail: BDUK and Freedom Fibre mutually agreed to terminate the Cheshire Project Gigabit contract.
Freedom Fibre received no public funding for the terminated Cheshire contract.
In February 2026 BDUK placed Cheshire premises into a new Openreach call-off eight contract.
Call-off eight awards £37.5 million to deliver gigabit-capable broadband to around 18,500 hard-to-reach Cheshire premises.

guard_streams.write_limit: Replacement award values and target counts are not evidence of present parcel serviceability.

guard_streams.source: BDUK North Shropshire Project Gigabit contract

facts.detail: Freedom Fibre's November 2023 North Shropshire award targeted 12,000 premises.
The page records 2,500 premises built and a historical aim for another 1,000 by the end of June 2025.
BDUK and Freedom Fibre agreed to remove the remaining 8,500 premises from that contract.
In April 2026 affected premises were included within Openreach call-off three covering other parts of Shropshire.

guard_streams.write_limit: Historical targets, descoping and replacement contracts require current build evidence before any parcel promotion.
